items.title: Delusion
items.reason: A six-episode Thai mystery thriller whose murder investigation keeps producing consequential information rather than merely accumulating procedure. The missing-child case becomes a murder inquiry, Pete uncovers an eerily similar older case, a second murder disrupts the working theory, Narong leads Wan to buried evidence, and the final investigation exposes incriminating material and the family's central secret. Investigation, clue-puzzling and culprit-hunt are therefore very strong, while revelation frequency and progressive revelation remain independently high because substantive discoveries arrive across the season and repeatedly change the picture. Family drama is substantial but does not displace the mystery engine.

items.title: Sender
items.reason: A 94-minute paranoid psychological mystery built around Julia trying to identify who is sending increasingly personal packages and whether she is being watched or manipulated. The film continuously introduces suspects, detours and paranoid possibilities, sustaining uncertainty about what can be trusted. Its investigation and clue structure are less rigorous than a procedural and its answers are intentionally messy, so revelation cadence and progressive revelation are held at moderate-high rather than maximal values; the strongest fit comes from mystery, suspense, unreliable perspective, surveillance and evidence/reality manipulation.
